hitl_conditions: Operators intervene only when the package twin raises excursion or status-violation alerts; task allocation and reputation updates execute autonomously via smart contracts; requesters set task reward and time constraints.
key_finding: Package digital twins (Arrhenius model) plus Random Forest predictions of UAV energy and delivery success, feeding a blockchain-hosted Gale-Shapley allocation, improve QoS by at least 37%, delivery success by at least 45%, worker reputation by 32% and payoff by 22% versus benchmarks; the RF energy model reaches MAE 1.66.

quotes.text: In the post-allocation phase, the framework monitors each package through its twin, which continuously mirrors the package’s physical state and generates data-driven performance feedback.
A critical yet often costly phase within this system is the last-mile delivery (LMD), the final step where goods are transported from a distribution center or local hub to the end customer [1].
In this work, an RF regressor model is trained to predict energy consumption, as it takes into consideration the features’ importance, scales efficiently, and achieves high accuracy.
quotes.section: 3.2.1 UAVs model: Proposed energy consumption prediction

quotes.text: Pre-trained ML models predict UAV energy requirements and GVs delivery success probabilities. These estimates generate Quality of Service (QoS) and Quality of Request (QoR) rankings for tasks and workers. A Gale–Shapley stable-matching algorithm then pairs tasks with workers.
It is hosted on the Ethereum blockchain to enable a secure and automated allocation and ensure platform data security and participants’ accountability.

This real-time simulation capability enables delivery operators to implement immediate corrective actions during temperature excursions and allow a transparent and trusted monitoring for the requesters.
